statements: Create aggregate.mjs at the workspace root: an ES module with one named function export, aggregate(ballots). Use Node.js built-ins only and no dependencies. Tests, if you write any, go under test/.

ballots must be an array of ballots; a ballot is an array of tiers, best tier first; a tier is an array of identifiers; an identifier is a string. Anything else, anywhere in the input, throws a TypeError whose code property is 'E_TYPE'. This check covers every ballot before the check of the next statement starts.

Only after the previous check has passed for all ballots: if one ballot names the same identifier twice, whether in one tier or in two different tiers, the function throws a TypeError whose code property is 'E_BALLOT'. The same identifier in different ballots is normal.

The candidates are the distinct identifiers over all ballots together; let C be their number. Within a ballot, a tier holding t identifiers whose earlier tiers in that ballot hold p identifiers in total receives the points C-1-p, C-2-p, down to C-p-t. Each identifier of the tier gets the plain average of those t points. An empty tier holds no identifiers and has no effect.

A candidate that a ballot does not name is unmentioned in it. If the ballot names M identifiers in total, all its unmentioned candidates together receive the points C-1-M, C-2-M, down to 0, and each of them gets the plain average of these points. A ballot with no identifiers at all therefore gives every candidate the same average.

A candidate's score is the exact arithmetic mean, over all ballots including those that do not name it, of the points it receives. It is reported as a fraction in lowest terms, as integers num and den with den greater than zero; a score of zero is num 0 and den 1. Rounded or approximate decimal values are wrong.

The result is an array with one object per candidate, each having exactly the properties id, num and den, ordered by score from highest to lowest; equal scores are ordered by id ascending, comparing strings by UTF-16 code unit values, so every uppercase ASCII letter comes before every lowercase one. With no ballots, or no candidates, the result is an empty array.
The function is pure: no I/O, no shared state, and the arguments are not mutated.
brief: Implement aggregate.mjs exactly as the numbered statements specify, then stop. Do not change any other file except tests under test/.
